column2: A New York subway station mezzanine seen head on: a long row of steel turnstiles with small red LED readers that all display PLEASE SWIPE AGAIN, a token booth with a clerk behind scratched glass, white tile walls with a green tile band and a mosaic sign that says COUNTED ST, commuters stuck at the turnstiles swiping yellow fare cards, one leaning on the bar in defeat, a thousand belt scratches on the steel, fluorescent light, wet grey floor.

The inside of a New York subway car looking straight down the length of the car: orange and yellow plastic seats, stainless steel poles, a dancer in a red tracksuit hanging horizontally from a pole mid spin, another mid flip with sneakers near the ceiling, seated commuters leaning away, a commuter asleep under a folded coat, a strip of advertising cards above the windows, the far door glowing, night outside the windows with motion blur, fluorescent light.

A New York subway platform in January: a crowd of commuters in winter coats, scarves, knit hats and formal shirts but no trousers, in boxer shorts and briefs and tights with dress socks and office shoes, reading newspapers and phones as if nothing is wrong, one commuter half hidden behind a shopping bag wearing ordinary khaki trousers, a train arriving with its headlights, steel columns painted green, white tile with a mosaic band, cold fluorescent light.

The main concourse of Grand Central Terminal: the celestial green ceiling with gold constellations, the four faced brass clock on the information booth, the grand staircase, tall arched windows pouring winter sunbeams with dust drifting in them, two hundred commuters frozen mid stride like statues, one bent to pick up a dropped folder, one mid bite of a sandwich, a coffee suspended mid pour, perfect stillness, Tennessee marble floor reflecting the light, January 2008.

The bottom of the staircase at the First Avenue L station seen from the platform at human eye level: concrete steps rising to a mezzanine, green painted steel railings, a brown rat on the third step dragging a whole slice of pizza bigger than itself by the crust, commuters stopped on the stairs around it giving it room, one filming with a phone, white tile walls with a 1 AV mosaic, fluorescent light, a wet floor, September 2015.

A SoHo street at dawn: a small French bakery with a pastel awning and a line of people wrapped around the block and out of sight, folding stools, blankets, paper coffee cups, phones on oversized battery packs, a velvet rope, a chalkboard that says SOLD OUT BY 8, pink pastry boxes, cast iron facades, fire escapes, cobblestones, the first sun hitting the top floors, May 2013.

A tiny New York studio apartment of 300 square feet seen from its front door: a clawfoot bathtub standing in the kitchen beside the stove, a loft bed built over the refrigerator, one window looking straight into a brick wall, a radiator painted silver, a folding bike on the wall, exposed pipes, a rent notice taped to the fridge that reads $4,250, a hot plate, crowded shelves, warm lamp light, intricate clutter.

A New York deli counter with a towering wall of soft drink cups and bottles, giant 64 ounce cups stacked like a monument, a hand painted sign that says 16 OZ MAX BY ORDER OF THE CITY, a cashier behind the counter, lottery tickets, a cat asleep on the counter, bags of chips hanging in rows, a fridge case glowing, intricate shelves of candy and gum, fluorescent light, 2012.

Bowling Green in Lower Manhattan: the massive bronze charging bull statue, and facing it a small bronze statue of a girl with her hands on her hips, and at her feet a small bronze pug lifting its leg, tourists taking photographs, police barriers, the curved granite facade of the old custom house behind, autumn trees, overcast light, cobblestones, March 2017.

Washington Square Park at the marble arch on an October afternoon: a huge crowd of young men who all wear the same brown jacket and have the same head, holding handwritten cardboard numbers, a folding table with a tiny trophy and a fifty dollar bill, police barricades, a brass band, phones held up everywhere, the fountain, autumn leaves, golden light, October 2024.

The Pond in Central Park in autumn: a small glowing orange, green and purple Mandarin duck on the water leaving a wake, and on the shore a packed crowd of photographers with enormous telephoto lenses and tripods, a man holding a cardboard sign that says HOT DUCK, the Gapstow stone bridge behind, midtown towers above the trees, fall foliage reflecting in the water, soft afternoon light, October 2018.

The High Line park at 30th Street with a colossal 16 foot hyperreal pigeon sculpture on a plinth above the walkway, grey with an iridescent neck, people tiny beneath it, hundreds of real pigeons on the railings and the planting, glass towers behind, wild grasses, old railway tracks in the planting, late afternoon light, 2024.

A Midtown Manhattan avenue in December at noon packed with thousands of people in cheap red Santa suits, elves, reindeer antlers, a Santa asleep on a fire hydrant, a bar with a line of Santas, a bus stop full of Santas, steam from a manhole, holiday lights, bright winter sun, high rise buildings on both sides receding into the distance.

Times Square at night from the red steps looking south: towering LED billboards that show the words NEW YORKERS and COUNTED and giant eye flowers, a crowd of costumed characters in furry suits and superhero costumes posing with tourists, a cowboy in white briefs and boots with an acoustic guitar, a hot dog cart, yellow cabs, wet asphalt reflecting every screen, dense, dazzling.

The steps of New York City Hall with a press conference podium in front, microphones, a brand new black wheeled trash bin with a lid on a pedestal under a spotlight like a product launch, a mountain of black trash bags on the curb beside it with rats on the bags, a banner that reads RAT CZAR, officials and reporters with cameras, a plush groundhog on a cushion, autumn light.

The inside of a New York bodega the night before a blizzard: shelves completely stripped bare except for one loaf of bread and a single carton of milk under a spotlight, a wall mounted TV showing a red weather map with the word HISTORIC, shoppers grabbing the last items, a hand written sign that says NO MORE SALT NO MORE SHOVELS, snow beginning outside the glass door, fluorescent light, January 2015.

The hot dog eating contest stage on the Coney Island boardwalk on the Fourth of July: a long table of competitors, hundreds of hot dogs in buns stacked in front of them, cups of water for dunking buns, giant digital counters above each competitor reading numbers near 70, red white and blue bunting, a roaring crowd, the Wonder Wheel and the Cyclone roller coaster behind, a hot bright summer sky, confetti.
